RegexTokenizer: Default token arguments are not mapped to vocabulary index
The ID's of the default special tokens in RegexTokenizer  are set here:

https://github.com/NVIDIA/NeMo/blob/72d78d832c6332ccc7f44811fb777eb7044df1d8/nemo/collections/common/tokenizers/regex_tokenizer.py#L75-L82

However, the constructor, allows custom special tokens:

https://github.com/NVIDIA/NeMo/blob/72d78d832c6332ccc7f44811fb777eb7044df1d8/nemo/collections/common/tokenizers/regex_tokenizer.py#L42-L51


So this could cause issues (specifically extra unknowns) when text is converted to tokens, then to ids, then back.
</issue>

            sep_token: token used for separating sequences

I have analyzed the issue in `nemo/collections/common/tokenizers/regex_tokenizer.py`.

The problem was that the `RegExTokenizer.__init__` method initialized its internal vocabulary using the hardcoded `DEFAULT_*` constants, even if the user provided custom values for `mask_token`, `bos_token`, `eos_token`, `pad_token`, `sep_token`, or `unk_token`. This discrepancy meant that the mapping between tokens and IDs was incorrect when custom special tokens were used, potentially leading to incorrect tokenization/detokenization or unexpected unknown tokens.

I have updated the `__init__` method to use the instance attributes (e.g., `self.pad_token`, `self.unk_token`, etc.) when building the `self.vocab` dictionary. This ensures that the vocabulary correctly reflects the tokens provided by the user.

```python
        # initialize with default vocab
        self.vocab = {
            self.pad_token: 0,  # pad_token
            self.unk_token: 1,  # unk_token
            self.bos_token: 2,  # begin_token
            self.eos_token: 3,  # end_token
            self.mask_token: 4,  # mask_token
            self.sep_token: 5,  # sep_token
        }
```

Additionally, the `_update_cache` method already uses `self.unk_token` to determine `self._unk_id`, so this change ensures consistency across the class.
